title: Guarded node deployment scoping — Hearthstone Diagnostics
summary: Exploratory scoping call focused on on-prem, air-gapped deployment for regulated diagnostic inference. Covered update mechanics for offline environments, hardware/thermal constraints, KMS/HSM strategies for key injection, and SLA/rollout expectations. Decided to run a 6-week pilot (1 rack) with constrained model set and offline image updates; Redwood to provide security pack and pilot pricing.
action_items: Lena Park: Send security pack (SOC2 summary, deployment checklist, signed image verification doc) by 2026-10-04

Evan Cho: Share internal patch window policy and VIN for change control by 2026-10-05

transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date: 2026-09-30
- Start: 16:00 PDT
- Duration: ~54 minutes
- Location: Zoom (no external network to customer side)
- Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Gable (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood Solutions), Dr. Omar Ruiz (CTO, Hearthstone), Sofia Patel (Head Infra), Evan Cho (Security Lead), Maya Liu (ML Platform)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Customer is a regulated diagnostics lab wanting air-gapped inference nodes inside their private data center. Primary concerns: how updates happen without internet, how keys are managed, hardware power/thermal limits in their rack, and what minimal model set to pilot to validate latency/cost.

Transcript Body:
[00:00:00] Lena Park: Hey everyone, thanks for carving the time — quick intro from our side, I'm Lena, AE for Redwood Inference, with Marcus our systems SE and Priya on security integration.
[00:00:12] Dr. Omar Ruiz: Thanks, Lena. We appreciate you, we'll try to keep this focused. I'm Omar, CTO, we run the inference for biomarker scans, so obviously latency and fault tolerance is kinda important.
[00:00:22] Sofia Patel: Hi all, Sofia here. I run the infra team. Short background: our data center is locked down, no egress allowed from the test environment, airgapped. We patch via signed media only.
[00:00:31] Marcus Gable: Totally understood. We've done a few of these — so think signed artifacts, manual key injection, and offline telemetry to a jump host are common patterns. Curious about your update cadence and what's required by compliance for you.
[00:00:44] Evan Cho: We have a quarterly patch window for anything that touches PHI, sometimes emergency patches are allowed but they need CISO signoff. We also require HSM for any private keys, and we can't have private keys ever leave a tamper-evident module.
[00:00:58] Priya Nair: Okay good — we support HSM-backed key stores on our private deploy. Two typical options: customer-managed HSM (you inject keys) or we provide a signed image plus key-wrapping guidance. Which do you prefer?
[00:01:12] Evan Cho: Customer-managed HSM is required. We will not accept remote KMS calls.
[00:01:16] Marcus Gable: Got it. That maps nicely — our runtime can be configured to use local PKCS#11 HSM providers. For image updates we typically produce a signed tarball with a SHA256 manifest and code-signing certificate.
[00:01:28] Maya Liu: How do you handle rollback on those signed images? If a model update regresses, we need a safe, auditable rollback mechanism.
[00:01:34] Marcus Gable: We include versioned manifests and a signed ’rollback allowlist’ optionally. In practice, customers manage the gate — we can support immediate revert to previous container artifacts without network interaction. It is a manual step unless you choose to enable a signed policy that automates it during a patch window.
[00:01:50] Dr. Omar Ruiz: Okay, manual is fine for the pilot. We also care about compute choices — you're recommending H100? A100? We have thermal limits in our rack — 6U per node is the upper bound with a 10kW shared PDUs, and we can't change datacenter cooling easily.
[00:02:06] Marcus Gable: Right, that's critical. H100 gives better performance per watt for transformer workloads but depending on your power budget and availability we can size with A100 or even an RTX-like lower power option for the pilot. We'll model throughput in tokens/sec for each config.
[00:02:21] Sofia Patel: Our procurement probably goes for mid-range GPUs — we can reallocate one chassis for the pilot but it must be <7kW sustained. Also, the machines must be rack-mounted racks with limited rear-door cooling.
[00:02:33] Lena Park: Noted. For the pilot scope — what would success look like? Is it latency under X ms? Throughput Y requests/min? Accuracy/regression tolerances?
[00:02:42] Dr. Omar Ruiz: Success is twofold: functional — the model outputs match our existing on-prem golden set within a 2% delta on our eval metrics; operational — we can push signed updates in our quarterly window and perform a verified rollback. Latency target is 200ms p50 for single-chat-style calls, given our sequences are short (<=256 tokens).
[00:03:01] Maya Liu: And cost target? We have internal run-rate budgets and we need to compare Redwood Dedicated vs self-hosting.
[00:03:06] Lena Park: For a pilot we normally size for throughput and show expected unit economics. We'll include a comparison: Hosted (no), Dedicated (reserved), Private (air-gapped) — we can show per-token cost under your observed load. But the private on-prem pilot has different cost levers — batching, quantization, and KV caching all change the economics.
[00:03:21] Evan Cho: On quantization — do you support int8 or 4-bit quantization in the runtime and how does that interact with accuracy? Our models are sensitive to hallucination; we can't accept degraded outputs.
[00:03:30] Marcus Gable: We support quantized variants and we recommend running evals on your golden prompts. Often int8 is acceptable, O4/quant configs can preserve output quality with careful calibration. We'll ship quantized model artifacts for you to test offline.
[00:03:43] Sofia Patel: About telemetry and logs — we cannot send any inference telemetry out of the airgapped cluster. Is there a way to run the Redwood Console locally?
[00:03:51] Priya Nair: We offer a private control plane option that can be deployed into your VPC, and for airgapped setups we provide an on-prem Console image (no egress) with configurable retention. There's an agent that writes telemetry to an internal Elasticsearch or S3 replacement. We can also red-team the telemetry paths during the pilot.
[00:04:08] Evan Cho: Good. Also the legal team wants tamper evidence for any media we accept — do you support checksums and code-signing chain of custody?
[00:04:16] Marcus Gable: Yes, signed tarballs, signed manifests, checksum verification. We can also provide notarized signing if needed; we work with yubikey-backed signing keys.
[00:04:26] Dr. Omar Ruiz: One more thing — our change process requires a physical handoff for emergency patches sometimes, i.e., a USB with signed image delivered to our secure intake. Can Redwood produce images that can be validated offline easily?
[00:04:37] Lena Park: Yes, we have a runbook for media-based delivery — we will produce the signed image and attestations, and an HSM-backed signing certificate chain. We'll include instructions for verifying signatures with openssl/pkcs11.
[00:04:50] Maya Liu: On the runtime side, how are KV caches handled? If we want to do prefix-caching between calls, will the cache require network share?
[00:04:57] Marcus Gable: Cache is local — per-node KV cache. For multi-node consistency we can support an on-prem Redis but we can also leave caches local and accept slight cold-cache hits. For your pilot, local cache per node is the simplest and avoids any cross-node network dependencies.
[00:05:12] Sofia Patel: Any required OS/kernel versions? Our images are locked to an RHEL8 baseline.
[00:05:17] Marcus Gable: We support RHEL8, Ubuntu 20/22. The runtime needs kernel 4.18+ ideally for optimized GPU drivers; we'll share detailed system packages in the deployment checklist.
[00:05:29] Evan Cho: About licensing and audit logs — we need per-request traceability for 90 days, and immutable logs for audits. Can you sign each inference event or provide a verifiable log chain?
[00:05:40] Priya Nair: We can produce signed audit logs and chain them with hash chaining. We also integrate with customer SIEM solutions; for airgapped, we write logs to local WORM storage if required.
[00:05:53] Dr. Omar Ruiz: All sounds good. For the pilot timeline, we need the SOW and a short security appendix. If we like the pilot results, we'd expand to two racks and consider model co-tenancy.
[00:06:04] Lena Park: We'll draft a 6-week pilot SOW: week 0-1 hardware provisioning and kernel prep, week 2 runtime and model install with offline validation, week 3–4 observed traffic + evals, week 5 rollback/drill and compliance review, week 6 final report.
[00:06:19] Maya Liu: For the pilot we'll want a constrained model set; can you provide a small open model you're comfortable shipping with quantized variants?
[00:06:25] Marcus Gable: Yes — we'll suggest a family with 7B/13B variants that match your latency goals. We'll provide int8 builds and golden evals to run locally.
[00:06:35] Sofia Patel: Shipping questions: does Redwood require outbound ports during initial install for license activation? We cannot allow that.
[00:06:41] Priya Nair: No, for airgapped we do an offline license activation flow — signed license blobs that are applied via the same media as the image.
[00:06:48] Evan Cho: Great. Also, please include details about maintenance windows and rollback SLAs in the SOW.
[00:06:54] Lena Park: Will do. Any other major blockers we haven't covered?
[00:06:58] Dr. Omar Ruiz: Procurement timeline is variable but we can confirm rack allocation by 2026-10-12. Security team will review your pack.
[00:07:06] Lena Park: Perfect. We'll send a pilot SOW and security appendix; Marcus will follow up with hardware sizing options.
[00:07:13] Marcus Gable: I'll include perf estimates (p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec) for H100, A100, and an efficient lower-power config.
[00:07:20] Lena Park: Thank you everyone.
[00:07:22] Sofia Patel: Thanks.
[00:07:23] Evan Cho: Thanks all.

End of call notes (auto-timestamps approximate).

Observations/Notes from Redwood SE (post-call):
- Customer is high-compliance (medical diagnostics) — expect extended legal/security review.
- Airgapped constraints: offline license activation, media-based updates, customer-managed HSM required.
- Hardware constraints: <7kW sustained per rack, limited rear-door cooling, prefer fewer higher-efficiency GPUs (H100) but provisioning may go for A100 depending on procurement.
- Pilot recommendation: 1 rack, 2 nodes (or 3 small nodes) depending on model size; prioritize 7B/13B models quantized for initial validation.
